policy_title: Acupuncture for Chronic Lower Back Pain
rule_statement: Humana treats all services covered under the acupuncture for cLBP benefit furnished the same day as if they were furnished in one session. For 2022 and later, Humana MA plans cover up to 20 sessions per year. Therefore, Humana MA plans do not require providers to report modifier KX for charges for acupuncture visits 13 through 20 in any calendar year, despite CMS acupuncture billing guidance, for Original Medicare, about modifier KX billing. Note: For 2022 through 2025, the 20-session limitation does not apply to services rendered by the patient's primary care provider (PCP). For 2026, whether the 20-session limitation applies to services rendered by the patient's PCP varies by plan as follows: • For Humana Group MA plans, the 20-session limitation does not apply to services rendered by the patient's PCP. • For Humana Individual MA plans, the 20-session limitation does apply to services rendered by the patient's PCP.
trigger_conditions: if they were furnished in one session

rule_statement: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans allow medically necessary ground ambulance and fixed or rotary wing air ambulance services according to Original Medicare guidelines. Humana only reimburses for covered transportation and mileage charges. The amount allowed for transportation includes reimbursement for all other items and services provided. Humana does not make separate payment for such items and services, including but not limited to oxygen, drugs, extra attendants, supplies, electrocardiograms (ECG or EKG) and night differential. Ambulance transportation provided to a member while registered as an inpatient at a hospital or skilled nursing facility (SNF), if billed, must be included in the facility's related consolidated inpatient claim. Charges for transportation of an inpatient will only be considered for reimbursement within the adjudication of the inpatient stay itself. In some situations, Humana determines that, though transportation was medically necessary, the mode of transportation may not have been medically necessary, such as transportation by air. When Humana determines that transportation was medically necessary, but air transportation was not medically necessary, Humana allows ground ambulance rates for the transportation. Generally, reimbursement for ambulance mileage to a facility is limited to the distance from the place from which the patient was transported to the nearest appropriate facility. However, when Humana authorizes admission to a facility in advance, regardless of whether prior authorization is required, Humana reimburses for mileage for the related ambulance transportation to that facility. A provider should bill all of the coverable mileage with HCPCS code A0425, A0435 or A0436 . However, if a provider bills such mileage with HCPCS code A0888 , Humana will not reimburse that charge but will deny it to provider liability. If the facility did not obtain prior authorization from Humana for the related admission, a provider should bill mileage for transportation beyond the closest facility with HCPCS code A0888 . Humana will not reimburse that charge but will deny it to provider liability. Humana adjusts reimbursement of covered transportation and mileage charges when multiple patients are simultaneously transported in the same ambulance to the same destination, indicated by modifier GM . If two patients are transported, Humana allows 75 percent of the provider's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for transportation and 50 percent of the provider's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for mileage. If three patients are transported, Humana allows 60 percent of the provider's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for transportation and a prorated percent of the provider's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for mileage, based on the number of patients on board. Note : Some Humana MA plans have supplemental transportation benefits, which provide coverage of some transportation services that Original Medicare would not cover. Providers and members are advised to contact Humana to verify if a Humana MA plan has supplemental transportation benefits.
trigger_conditions: if billed, must be included in the facility's related consolidated inpatient claim

rule_statement: Humana requires the anesthesia service code to be appended, as appropriate, with modifier AA, AD, QK, QX, QY or QZ. For an allowed anesthesia charge submitted with modifiers AA, QK, QX, QY or QZ , Humana plans allow the following percentage of the provider's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan : Note: Reimbursement of an anesthesia charge shall not exceed 100 percent of the total amount allowed for a single service reported on multiple providers' claims, such as when an anesthesiologist directs a nonphysician anesthetist. Additionally, for any coverable single anesthesia service, Humana plans allow no more than one anesthesiologist charge and allow no more than one nonphysician anesthetist charge. Humana calculates the reimbursement of an allowed anesthesia charge submitted with modifier AD with three base units, regardless of the base value units of the procedure code, multiplied by the conversion factor. One additional unit is considered when documentation confirms the supervising physician was present at induction. Additional units for length of time, qualifying circumstances codes or physical status modifiers are not allowed. Monitored anesthesia care must be indicated using modifier G8, G9 or QS , with the monitored anesthesia care modifier reported after modifier AA, AD, QK, QX, QY or QZ .

rule_statement: A medically necessary anesthesia procedure, such as an epidural injection or nerve block, administered with the intent to manage post-operative pain, may be reimbursed separately when the adequacy of the intra-operative anesthesia is not dependent on the epidural injection or nerve block. All the following requirements must be satisfied to qualify for separate reimbursement from the intra-operative anesthesia: • Medical record documentation of the post-operative pain management procedure must: - Be separate from the anesthesia record - Confirm the procedure was for post-operative pain management and the adequacy of the intra-operative anesthesia is not dependent on the epidural injection or nerve block - Include details about the procedure itself - Confirm the surgeon requested the anesthetist administer the procedure - Confirm the patient consented to the post-operative pain management plan and procedure • The time spent placing or administering a post-operative pain management procedure cannot be included in the intra-operative anesthesia time. • Modifier 59, XE or XU must be appended to the post-operative pain management procedure code to indicate a distinct procedural service was performed. • Post-operative pain management procedures may be administered pre-operatively, intra-operatively or post-operatively. Post-operative pain management procedures are not separately reimbursed when reported by the same physician reporting the procedure or surgical charge.
trigger_conditions: when the adequacy of the intra-operative anesthesia is not dependent on the epidural injection or nerve block

rule_statement: Original Medicare (OM) covers an assistant at surgery service provided by a physician, with some exclusions, or an NPP. Humana uses the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File assistant at surgery indicator to determine if an assistant at surgery is medically necessary and, therefore, covered. When the MPFS Relative Value File is not definitive, then Humana's internal criteria are used.

rule_statement: Only one of the following modifiers should be billed per charge: AS, 80, 81 or 82 . Humana will not reimburse a practitioner who acts as an assistant at surgery in a cesarean delivery any more than the assistant at surgery rate that would apply for the CPT code appropriate for delivery only.

rule_statement: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans allow claims for healthcare services provided due to automobile and workplace injuries according to applicable Medicare Secondary Payer (MSP) guidelines. A provider must make all reasonable efforts to determine whether there is other coverage for an automobile or workplace injury, such as under automobile or workers' compensation insurance, and must promptly report as described below, in claims submitted to Humana, and any such other coverage that is identified. Additionally, a provider must bill a patient's automobile or workplace injury insurance plan, if applicable, before billing the patient's Humana MA plan. Finally, a provider must promptly forward to Humana any determination by an automobile or workplace insurance plan made with respect to a claim for a Humana MA enrollee's injuries. A provider's failure to promptly fulfill any requirement could affect Humana's disposition of a claim after initial receipt and/or after initial adjudication. Humana expects providers to abide by the MSP billing requirements when submitting claims to Humana MA plans. If a provider identifies automobile insurance, the provider must include the information below when submitting a paper claim to Humana, or equivalent information when submitting an electronic claim to Humana. For a CMS-1500 form or its electronic equivalent: • Enter "yes" in box 10-B • Enter the accident date in field 14 • Enter all diagnosis codes in section 21 • Attach the following to the claim, if available: - Copy of the check from the primary insurance carrier - Copy of the explanation of benefits (EOB) from the primary insurance carrier - Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier - Personal injury protection (PIP) worksheet, if available - Statement from the patient indicating no PIP coverage, if applicable For a UB-04 form or its electronic equivalent: • Enter occurrence code 01 or 02, as applicable, and the accident date in fields 33 - 35 • Enter value code 14 in fields 39 - 41 • Enter all diagnosis codes in fields 67 - 76 • Attach the following to the claim, if available: - Copy of the check from the primary insurance carrier - Copy of the EOB from the primary insurance carrier - Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier - Statement from the patient indicating no PIP coverage, if applicable If a provider identifies workers' compensation insurance, the provider must include the information below when submitting a paper claim to Humana, or equivalent information when submitting an electronic claim to Humana. For a CMS-1500 form or its electronic equivalent: • Enter "yes" in box 10-B • Enter the accident date in field 14 • Enter all diagnosis codes in section 21 • Attach the following to the claim, if available: - Copy of the check from the primary insurance carrier - Copy of the EOB from the primary insurance carrier - Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier - Statement from the patient confirming that their employer does not provide workers' compensation coverage For a UB-04 form or its electronic equivalent: • Enter occurrence code 04 and accident date in fields 33 - 35 • Enter condition code 02, 05, or 77, as applicable, in fields 18 - 28 • Enter value code 15 or 41, as applicable, in fields 39 - 41 • Enter all diagnosis codes in fields 67 - 76 • Attach the following to the claim, if available: - Copy of the check from the primary insurance carrier - Copy of the EOB from the primary insurance carrier - Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier - Statement from the patient confirming that their employer does not provide workers' compensation coverage Note: Medicare benefits are secondary regardless of whether the patient wishes to file a workers' compensation claim. Humana may deny a claim for healthcare services provided due to an automobile or workplace injury if it is submitted without the information above. Humana may deny a claim when payment has been made, or when payment may reasonably be expected to be made, under any applicable liability insurance arrangement, including self-insurance, no-fault insurance or workers' compensation law or plan. Humana may also require providers to pursue and exhaust available no-fault insurance or workers' compensation coverage and to demonstrate reasonable efforts to exhaust any other applicable coverage, before submitting claims to Humana for payment. Note: For more guidance on the MSP provisions and billing requirements, see the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services' MSP booklet and the MSP manual in the References section of this policy.

policy_title: Chronic Care Management and Principal Care Management
rule_statement: guidance. That includes, but is not limited to, the criteria outlined below. Member Pre-Condition For PCM services, the member must be diagnosed with one chronic condition that places the patient at significant risk of death, acute exacerbation/decompensation or functional decline or that is expected to last at least 3 months or until the death of the patient. For CCM services, the member must be diagnosed with at least two chronic conditions that place the patient at significant risk of death, acute exacerbation/decompensation or functional decline and that are expected to last at least 12 months or until the death of the patient. Staff Requirement PCM and CCM services must be performed by clinical staff meeting the requirements of auxiliary personnel as defined by 42 CFR 410.26(a)(1). Billing Limitations A provider may not simultaneously bill for PCM services and certain other services, including CCM, for the same member. A provider may not bill for PCM services during the surgical global period of a service for which they are reimbursed for the same member. Only one provider may bill for CCM services for a specific member per month. CCM services for a specific member must be billed for either CCM or complex CCM, but not both, per month. A provider may not bill for CCM services rendered to a member during an inpatient facility stay that is coverable by the member's MA plan.
trigger_conditions: Applicable to Chronic Care Management and Principal Care Management services under Medicare Advantage.
exceptions_overrides: Standard payer clinical claim editing rules apply; no automated bypass.

rule_statement: Humana adjudicates a claim for services provided to a plan member based on the information submitted in that claim and information related to that claim. If a qualified healthcare provider disagrees with Humana's adjudication of that claim, based on the information submitted in that claim, that provider may submit to Humana a request for a dispute review of the plan's determination. If a provider submits a request for a dispute review timely and with all required information, Humana will review the claim to determine whether to revise the adjudication. Humana plans may use medical records and other available relevant documentation to review a dispute . This policy establishes the applicable timeframe for a qualified healthcare provider submission of a dispute request. Note : A corrected claim is a provider's submission of information that constitutes a material change to an existing claim. A claim submission that constitutes a material change to an existing claim is not a disagreement about Humana's adjudication of the claim as based on the information in the previous claim submission. Therefore, Humana plans will not review a corrected claim as a dispute .
trigger_conditions: If a qualified healthcare provider disagrees with Humana's adjudication of that claim, based on the information submitted in that claim, that provider may submit to Humana a request for a dispute review of the plan's determination

rule_statement: Unless otherwise stated in the contract, an in-network qualified healthcare provider may submit a dispute request within 18 months from the receipt of the original claim determination. An out-of-network qualified healthcare provider does not have a contractual relationship with a particular plan that would afford that qualified healthcare provider direct rights against that plan. An out-of-network qualified healthcare provider lacks, for example, the right to submit a claim, the right to require the plan to process a claim seeking a member's plan or policy benefits, the right to submit a dispute request and the right to submit corrected claims . Those examples are not exhaustive. Without waiving any provisions that prohibit an out-of-network qualified healthcare provider from assuming an enrollee's direct rights against the plan, a plan will allow an out-of-network qualified healthcare provider to submit a dispute request within: • The timeframe established by state or federal laws, or • 180 days from the receipt of the original claim determination when the applicable state and federal laws are silent.
trigger_conditions: when the applicable state and federal laws are silent

rule_statement: • Corrected claim: A claim that replaces a previously submitted claim and includes material information that differs from information included in the previously submitted claim. For this purpose, "material information" is information that, because it differs from information included in the previously submitted claim, could cause some change in reimbursement if that information were considered. • Dispute: A disagreement about a previous claim determination that does not entail a change to the material information submitted for that claim. The dispute must be presented in writing, challenging the potentially adverse determination of the claim based on the previously submitted information. Medical notes, industry standards and/or Original Medicare guidelines may be used to support a dispute request. • Qualified healthcare provider: A provider who is licensed by the appropriate state agency to diagnose or treat a sickness or bodily injury and provide preventive services.

rule_statement: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Some members are cost-share protected under federal law, meaning that providers must not collect from those members the calculated cost-sharing for covered services. Though the collection of cost-sharing from a member might be forbidden, if there is a payer subsequent to Humana, it might be possible to collect that cost-sharing from that subsequent payer. Humana uses remittance advice remark codes (RARCs) to indicate that members are cost-share protected. For example, a specific RARC's definition might be, "Alert: Patient is a Medicaid/ Qualified Medicare Beneficiary . Review your records for any wrongfully collected deductible. This amount may be billed to a subsequent payer." A provider should note when a Humana electronic remittance advice (ERA) includes such a RARC and react to it appropriately.
trigger_conditions: if there is a payer subsequent to Humana, it might be possible to collect that cost-sharing from that subsequent payer
exceptions_overrides: Standard payer clinical claim editing rules apply; no automated bypass.

rule_statement: Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans generally allow DME according to the applicable Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidance. Except where guidance in this policy differs from Original Medicare, providers should follow the applicable CMS guidance. For a DME item that can be rented or purchased, whether that item is rented or purchased is subject to any applicable referral or prior authorization determination. For a DME item that can be rented, when the Medicare Durable Medical Equipment, Prosthetics, Orthotics and Supplies (DMEPOS) Fee Schedule has no rental rate for that item, Humana will apply a contracted rental rate, where applicable. If there is no contracted rental rate, Humana may allow the item at the purchase rate. For a DME item that can be purchased, the amount allowed is affected by which purchase modifier is reported. • If a charge for a covered DME item is submitted with modifier NU , the amount allowed is the new equipment purchase rate. • If a charge for a covered DME item is submitted with modifier UE , the amount allowed is the used equipment purchase rate. The amount allowed for purchased used equipment is a reduced rate, typically 75%, of the new equipment purchase rate. Reimbursement for the DME item includes reimbursement for delivery and set-up. Humana does not reimburse separately for delivery and set-up. Reimbursement for covered services provided to an MA member is subject to the same special pricing rules that would apply for covered services provided to Original Medicare enrollees. For example, if a covered service provided to an Original Medicare enrollee would be priced using the Competitive Bidding Program rate, then that service provided to a Humana MA member in the same competitive bidding area is reimbursed using the same rate.

rule_statement: Humana requires an appropriate capped rental modifier and transaction modifier . Humana determines the amount allowed based on the transaction modifier billed for an item categorized as a capped rental DME item as described below. Rental If a charge for a covered capped rental DME item is submitted with modifier RR , the amount allowed is the monthly rental rate, as described below. Rental is allowed for a period of continuous use not to exceed 13 months. Reimbursement to a provider whose contract is not based on the Medicare DMEPOS Fee Schedule is allowed at the contracted rental rate. Otherwise, Humana allows an item, other than a power wheelchair, at a monthly rental rate of 10% of the item's purchase rate for each of the first three months and then 7.5% of the purchase rate for the remainder of the rental period. For a power wheelchair, Humana allows at a monthly rental rate of 15% of the item's purchase rate for the first three months and then 6% of the purchase rate for the remainder of the rental period. In both scenarios, the monthly rental rate is based on the purchase rate in effect for the date of service billed. A capped rental DME item is considered purchased after 13 continuous months of covered rental. rule_statement: Humana may reimburse the replacement of a DME base item, part or accessory after the expiration of the RUL if it is still medically necessary but no longer functional. The RUL period begins the first date of service when the specific base item, part or accessory was individually reimbursed. Additionally, the following criteria must be met: • The maximum number of allowed units has not been exceeded. • The cost to replace a part or accessory, including labor and parts, does not exceed the cost of renting or purchasing a new base item. • Base item, part or accessory replacement is not due to intentional damage, neglect or misuse of equipment. • Replacement of a part or accessory is only allowed for a member if the same member owns the base item. • The base item, part or accessory must not be under warranty. Documentation of an expired or denied warranty is required, upon request. • The base item, part or accessory is not currently being rented. Replacement Prior to the Expiration of the RUL In addition to the relevant requirements outlined above, the following conditions apply to replacement of a DME base item, part or accessory before expiration of the RUL. Modifier RA Humana may reimburse the replacement of a base item, part or accessory before expiration of the RUL only if either of the following scenarios are true: • The member's medical needs have changed such that a different item is medically necessary; or • The item was lost, stolen or unintentionally damaged beyond repair. For only the first charge for the replacement item, modifier RA must be billed with the Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) code for a base item, part or accessory replaced for one of the scenarios described above. Modifier RB Humana may reimburse the replacement of a part or accessory in association with the covered repair of a base item before the expiration of the RUL of the part or accessory when the following criteria are met: • The part or accessory is not an upgrade to the base item. • Replacement is necessary to make the base item functional. • The part or accessory is not billed on the same date of service as the base item. • The base item is not categorized as Frequently Serviced or Oxygen Equipment. • A charge for the base item was not previously denied. • The base item was previously purchased, including an item for which payment has capped through rental payments. • Modifier RR is not also billed. • Box 19 on the claim form or its electronic equivalent includes the base item code and purchase date. Modifier RB must be billed with the HCPCS code for that replaced part or accessory. When all requirements are met, the replacement of a part or accessory will be allowed at the purchase rate.
trigger_conditions: if it is still medically necessary but no longer functional

policy_title: Dental Services Inextricably Linked to Medical Services
rule_statement: Dental services are generally not covered by the Medicare Program's basic benefits. However, one exception for this coverage exclusion is for dental services that are inextricably linked to the clinical success of a covered medical service. In such cases, there must also be exchange of information, or integration, between the medical professional and the dentist. This policy establishes Humana's billing requirements and reimbursement for dental services that are inextricably linked to the clinical success of a covered medical service.

policy_title: Initial Preventive Physical Examination and Annual Wellness Visit
rule_statement: According to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, an initial preventive physical examination (IPPE), also known as the "Welcome to Medicare" preventive visit, is a one-time introductory visit provided during the first 12 months a Medicare beneficiary has Part B benefits. The visit may include, but is not limited to, the following: • A review of a beneficiary's medical and health-related social history. • Education and counseling about preventive services, including certain screenings, shots and referrals for other care, if needed. • Other services, such as a written plan letting the beneficiary know what preventive services the beneficiary needs. If a beneficiary has had Part B benefits for longer than 12 months, the beneficiary can receive an annual wellness visit (AWV) to develop or update a personalized prevention plan to prevent disease and disability based on the beneficiary's current health and risk factors. The following policy outlines Humana's reimbursement for claims for an IPPE and AWV.

Humana Medicare Advantage plans reimburse a charge for: • An IPPE service, HCPCS code G0402 , once per lifetime and only if provided within the first 12 months after the effective date of the member's first Medicare Part B coverage period. • An initial AWV service, HCPCS code G0438 , once per lifetime beginning in the calendar year following the IPPE. However, the initial AWV is not dependent on reimbursement of an earlier IPPE. • A subsequent AWV service, HCPCS code G0439 , once per calendar year beginning in the calendar year following an allowed charge for HCPCS code G0438 . However, a subsequent AWV is not dependent on reimbursement of an earlier AWV or IPPE. Humana limits reimbursement of HCPCS codes G0402, G0438 and G0439 to only one of these services per calendar year.

rule_statement: Humana's Medicare Advantage plans follow the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidelines for inpatient Part B re- billing. When an acute care hospital determines before discharge that the patient should not have been admitted as an inpatient, Humana will only accept services submitted on an appropriate outpatient TOB 13x or 85x claim ; and will allow the provider to submit all codes that, for a normal outpatient situation, could be appropriate for that TOB; and requires condition code 44 . An inpatient claim should not be submitted. When an acute care hospital or Humana determines after discharge that the patient should not have been admitted as an inpatient, Humana will only accept services submitted on an inpatient Part B TOB 12x claim. The billing should reflect the reasonable and necessary Part B services and provide the correct Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) and Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) codes when available. Report condition code W2 to indicate that this is a Part B claim and include "A/B Rebilling" in the treatment authorization field. For preadmission services in the 3-day payment window , a hospital may separately bill for services provided prior to an inpatient admission and should report "A/B Rebilling" in the treatment authorization field of the appropriate outpatient TOB 13x or 85x claim . Note : When a facility fails to obtain a required inpatient authorization or the authorization request is denied, the facility must bill emergency-related services provided before the inpatient admission separately from the inpatient services. For an inpatient admission that requires authorization, Humana will deny an inpatient claim that includes unauthorized inpatient services, including charges for preadmission emergency-related services. When billed on inpatient Part B claims or outpatient claims, some services may require specific authorization.

policy_title: Itemized Bill Review for Inpatient Routine Services
rule_statement: Facility billing guidelines for the UB-04 claim form, also known as the CMS-1450, and the 837 institutional electronic equivalent require providers to bill revenue codes to describe services rendered. Revenue codes are categorical and do not describe exact items, supplies and services provided during an inpatient admission. Humana may request an itemized bill for an inpatient facility claim to verify that billed revenue codes represent charges for appropriately billed items, supplies and services. Routine items, supplies and services already included in the primary inpatient room and board charge are not separately billable. Medicare Advantage Payment Policy Medicare Advantage Payment Policy In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana sometimes reviews an itemized bill for an inpatient admission to determine whether supplies, items and services specified on the itemized bill are separately billable. To separately bill for items, supplies and services rendered during an inpatient hospital encounter, the provider must consistently follow its customary charging practices for all Medicare and non-Medicare patients, for all payers and health plans. The following supplies, items and services are typically not separately billable and, therefore, not separately payable from the general room and board charge or primary service charge. Please note that the examples given do not represent an exhaustive list. • Any supplies, items and services that, under customary charging practices , are included in charges for a specific service or in charges for the delivery of services in a specific location. Examples of included supplies and items are bandages and inpatient admission kits. Examples of included services are IV flushing, dressing changes, equipment monitoring and routine nursing care and assessments. • All items and supplies that may be purchased over the counter, such as personal care items, ice packs, alcohol wipes and cotton balls. • All reusable items, supplies and equipment that are provided to all patients on a routine basis during an inpatient admission; this applies to all types of inpatient admissions, including an admission to a specific treatment area, such as a NICU or CCU, and applies to the admission of a patient who is receiving the same types of service as a patient in a specific treatment area. Examples of reusable items, supplies and equipment are cardiac monitors and durable medical equipment (DME) items used while inpatient.

rule_statement: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Bacterial culture testing (CPT code 87081, CPT code 87070, CPT code 87071) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE in cases of viral pharyngitis. • Amplification testing (CPT code 87651) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE in cases of viral pharyngitis. • Rapid antigen diagnostic testing (RADT) (CPT code 87880) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE for any of the following: - As a follow-up test to bacterial culture test (CPT code 87081, CPT code 87070, CPT code 87071) for a Streptococcal infection within the prior 14 days - In cases of viral pharyngitis • Serological titer testing (CPT code 86060, CPT code 86215) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE in patients with Streptococcus . • Direct probe testing (CPT code 87650) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE if amplification testing (CPT code 87651) for Streptococcus has been performed on the same date of service. • The following tests ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE in patients with Streptococcus or Enterococcus : - Anti-streptolysin O immunoassay (CPT code 86060, CPT code 86063) - Tests that screen and identify multiple Streptococcal strains, using either immunoassay or nucleic acid-based assays, such as the Solana Strep Complete Assay and the Lyra Direct Strep Assay (CPT code 83789, CPT code 87430) • The quantification of any strain of Streptococcus using nucleic acid amplification, including polymerase chain reaction (PCR), (CPT code 87652) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE.

policy_title: Laboratory - Biochemical Markers of Alzheimer's Disease and Dementia
rule_statement: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • For individuals with a diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment or dementia, measurement of the following biomarkers IS REIMBURSABLE: - Amyloid beta peptides (CPT Code 82233, CPT code 82234, CPT code 0358U) - The ratio (CPT code 0459U) of total tau (t-tau) (CPT code 84394) to amyloid beta 1-42 (Aβ42) (CPT code 82234) - The ratio (CPT code 0445U) of phosphorylated tau 181 (p-tau181) (CPT code 84393) to Aβ42 (CPT code 82234) - The ratio of p-tau 217 (p-tau217) (CPT code 84393, CPT code 0479U) to Aβ42 (CPT code 82234) • When not ordered in conjunction with Aβ42 (CPT code 82234), measurement of the following biomarkers IS NOT REIMBURSABLE: - t-tau (CPT code 84394) - p-tau181 (CPT code 84393) - p-tau217 (CPT code 84393, CPT code 0479U) • For individuals with a diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment or dementia, measurement of other biomarkers (CPT code 83520, CPT code 83884, CPT code 0547U) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE. • For individuals with a diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment or dementia, measurement of all other cerebral spinal fluid biomarkers (CPT code 0393U, CPT code 0443U, CPT code 0548U) or plasma biomarkers (CPT code 0479U, CPT code 0551U) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE. • The use of DISCERNTM (CPT code 0206U*, CPT code 0207U*) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE. • The use of other multianalyte assays (CPT code 0412U*, CPT code 0503U*, CPT code 0568U*, CPT code 0596U) for Alzheimer's disease or dementia IS NOT REIMBURSABLE. • Gene expression profiling to predict development of Alzheimer's disease (CPT code 0289U**) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE.

policy_title: Laboratory - Biomarkers for Myocardial Infarction and Chronic Heart Failure
rule_statement: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Quantitative measurement of cardiac troponin T or I (CPT code 84484) for the diagnosis of myocardial infarction (MI) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals presenting with any of the following: - Ischemic chest pain - Pain in the upper abdomen, shoulders, upper arms, forearms, wrists, fingers, neck and throat, lower jaw and teeth or back pain - Shortness of breath, belching, nausea, indigestion, vomiting, diaphoresis, dizziness, lightheadedness, clamminess or fatigue - Squeezing, tightness, pressure, constriction, crushing, strangling, burning, heartburn, fullness in the chest, band-like sensation, knot in the center of the chest, lump in throat, ache, heavy weight on chest or toothache when there is radiation to the lower jaw • A maximum of four serial quantitative troponin tests (CPT code 84484) IS REIMBURSABLE in the first three days after presentation. • Testing for natriuretic peptide, such as B-Type Natriuretic Peptide (BNP) or N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide (NT- proBNP) (CPT code 83880*) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals presenting with dyspnea or shortness of breath. • Testing for BNP or NT-proBNP (CPT code 83880*) IS REIMBURSABLE every rolling 12 months for individuals presenting with any of the following: - Acute or chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure - Chronic heart failure: systolic, diastolic or combined systolic and diastolic - Chronic right heart failure • Measurement of the following cardiac biomarkers for the diagnosis or prognosis of MI IS NOT REIMBURSABLE in conjunction with the measurement of cardiac troponin T or I: Policy Number : LAB2023001 - Cardiac creatine kinase isoenzyme myocardial band (CK-MB) (CPT code 82553, CPT code 82554) - Copeptin (CPT code 84588) - C-reactive protein (CPT code 86140) - Creatine kinase (CK) (CPT code 82550) - CK isoenzymes (CPT code 82552) - Heart-type fatty acid binding protein (H-FABP) (CPT code 82725) - Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) (CPT code 83625) - Myoglobin (CPT code 83874) • For individuals with signs and symptoms of acute coronary syndrome, quantitative measurement of cardiac troponin T or I (CPT code 84484) by an independent laboratory IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • In the outpatient setting, qualitative measurement of cardiac troponin T or I (CPT code 84512) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • In the outpatient setting, testing of growth stimulation expressed gene 2 (ST2) or its isoforms (CPT code 83006) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . rule_statement: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. Diabetes mellitus - Disorder of galactose, lipoprotein, or amino acid transport metabolism - History of circulatory system disorders - Hypertriglyceridemia - Obesity or metabolic syndrome - Presence of coronary angioplasty implant • Once per lifetime measurement of lipoprotein (a) [Lp(a)] (CPT code 83695**) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals 18 years of age or older. • Measurement of homocysteine (CPT code 83090****) or conventional measurement of C-reactive protein (CPT code 86140) as a part of a risk assessment for cardiovascular disease (CVD) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Measurement of novel lipid and non-lipid biomarkers (CPT code 82610*, CPT code 83700**, CPT code 83701**, CPT code 83704**, CPT code 83719**, CPT code 83880***, CPT code 85384, CPT code 85415) as a part of a risk assessment for CVD IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Direct measurement of small dense low-density lipoprotein (LDL) (CPT code 83722) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE except in diagnoses of Cushings syndrome, chronic kidney disease (CKD), obstruction of the bile duct or pregnancy. • CVD risk panels consisting of multiple individual biomarkers intended to assess CVD (CPT code 0052U, CPT code 0308U**, CPT code 0309U**, CPT code 0415U**, CPT code 0541U**) ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE. • Measurement of lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2 (Lp-PLA2) (CPT code 83698****) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • All other biomarker panels designed to detect CVD risk (CPT code 0019M**, CPT code 0377U) ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE. • Measurement of components of a lipid panel (CPT code 82465*****, CPT code 83718*****, and CPT code 84478*****) ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE on the same date of service as a lipid panel (CPT code 80061*****).

rule_statement: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • For individuals with a diagnosis of either type 1 or type 2 diabetes, measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS REIMBURSABLE once every three months. • For individuals with a diagnosis of prediabetes, annual screening for type 2 diabetes with a measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS REIMBURSABLE. • Screening for prediabetes or type 2 diabetes with a measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS REIMBURSABLE once every 3 years in individuals 18 years of age and older with any of the following: - Cardiovascular disease - Family history of diabetes - High-risk race/ethnicity (e.g., African American, Latino or Hispanic, Native American, Asian American or Pacific Islander) at risk for type 2 diabetes (e.g., obesity) - History of gestational diabetes - Hypercholesterolemia - Hypertension - Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) - Metabolic syndrome - Other clinical conditions associated with insulin resistance (e.g., acanthosis nigricans) - Overweight or obese - Physical inactivity - Polycystic ovary syndrome • Screening for diabetes with an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) (CPT code 82951, CPT code 82952) or measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS REIMBURSABLE once every 3 years for children ages 10 - 17 with at least one of the following: - Acanthosis nigricans - Dyslipidemia - Family history of type 2 diabetes - Hypertension - Overweight or obese - Polycystic ovary syndrome • For individuals 10 years of age or older who have been diagnosed with cystic fibrosis (CF), screening for CF-related diabetes with an OGTT (CPT code 82951, CPT code 82952) IS REIMBURSABLE once every 365 days. • For pregnant individuals, an OGTT (CPT code 82951, CPT code 82952) IS REIMBURSABLE up to once per month during pregnancy.

rule_statement: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • The following tests ARE REIMBURSABLE for any of these conditions: bleeding, inflammation, itching, pain, pelvic infection, pregnancy with history of pre-term labor, redness and vaginitis: - Aptima® BV Assay (CPT code 81513**) - BD MAXTM Vaginal Panel (CPT code 81514**) - Direct probe deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) based identification of Gardnerella (CPT code 87510*), Trichomonas (CPT code 87660*) and Candida (CPT code 87480*) - Nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) or polymerase chain reaction (PCR) based identification of Gardnerella vaginalis (CPT code 87511*, CPT code 87512*) - NAAT or PCR based identification (CPT code 87661*) of Trichomonas vaginalis - PCR based identification of Candida (CPT code 87481*, CPT code 87482*) - Testing for the presence of amines (CPT code 82120) - Xpert® Xpress Mutliplex Vaginal Panel (MVP) (CPT code 81515***) • Screening for Trichomonas (CPT code 87660*, CPT code 87661*) IS REIMBURSABLE for any of the following risk factors: - Exchange of sex for payment - History of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) - Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) - Incarceration - Injection drug use - New or multiple partners • For asymptomatic individuals, including asymptomatic pregnant individuals at an average or high risk for premature labor, screening for trichomoniasis or bacterial vaginosis (CPT code 87480*, CPT code 87510*, CPT code 87661*) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Rapid identification of Trichomonas by enzyme immunoassay (CPT code 87808) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . rule_statement: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS ONLY REIMBURSABLE for individuals with a diagnosis of either Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes once every three months. • Measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS ONLY REIMBURSABLE once every 365 days to help in the detection and diagnosis of Type 2 diabetes in individuals aged 18 and over with any of the following: - Overweight or obese - Pre-diabetes - History of gestational diabetes - Family history of diabetes - Cardiovascular disease - Hypertension - Hypercholesterolemia - Metabolic syndrome - Polycystic ovary syndrome - High-risk race/ethnicity (e.g., African American, Latino or Hispanics, Native American, Asian American, Pacific Islanders) at risk for Type 2 diabetes (e.g., obesity) - Physical inactivity - Other clinical conditions associated with insulin resistance (e.g., acanthosis nigricans) • Diabetes screening with a hemoglobin A1c determination (CPT code 83037) IS ONLY REIMBURSABLE once every 3 years for children aged 10-17 with at least one of the following characteristics: - Overweight or obese - Family history of type 2 diabetes - Hypertension - Dyslipidemia - Polycystic ovary syndrome • Measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS ONLY REIMBURSABLE for pregnant individuals up to once per month during pregnancy. • Measurement of hemoglobin A1c (CPT code 83037) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE when billed in conjunction with measurement of (CPT code 82985) fructosamine.

rule_statement: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Measurement of serum free testosterone based on total serum testosterone (CPT code 84403**), sex hormone binding globulin (SHBG) (CPT code 84270) or bioavailable testosterone (CPT code 84410*) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals with any of the following conditions: - Acromegaly - Acute and chronic kidney failure - Benign prostatic hypertrophy - Cirrhosis or hepatitis - Diabetes mellitus - Erectile dysfunction - Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) disease - Hyperthyroidism - Hypothyroidism - Infertility - Nephrotic syndrome - Obesity - Polymorphisms - Use of estrogens - Use of glucocorticoids, progestins or androgenic steroids • Testing for serum total testosterone measurements (CPT code 84403**) IS REIMBURSABLE at the designated frequency in any of the following situations: - For individuals taking enzyme inhibitors for prostate cancer: as needed - For individuals receiving testosterone replacement therapy: up to eight tests every four years - Gender-dysphoric or gender-incongruent persons: as needed - Infertility: as needed - Symptomatic individuals being evaluated for polycystic ovary syndrome or functional hypothalamic amenorrhea: as needed • Measurement of serum dihydrotestosterone (CPT code 82642) IS REIMBURSABLE for diagnosing 5-alpha reductase deficiency in individuals with ambiguous genitalia, hypospadias or microphallus. • Measurement of serum estradiol (CPT code 82670, CPT code 82681) IS REIMBURSABLE for the following conditions at the designated frequency: - For individuals with gynecomastia: once per lifetime - For individuals who are experiencing infertility: as needed • Testing for serum total testosterone (CPT code 84403**), free testosterone (CPT code 84402) or bioavailable testosterone (CPT code 84410*) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE in asymptomatic individuals or in individuals with non-specific symptoms.

rule_statement: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Measurement of either serum lipase (CPT code 83690) or amylase (CPT code 82150) concentration for the initial diagnosis of acute pancreatitis IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals presenting with any of the following signs and symptoms: - Abdominal distention - Abdominal pain - Abnormal weight loss - Acute pancreatitis - Anorexia - Cullen sign - Diarrhea - Fever - Grey Turner sign - Hypoactive bowel sounds - Hypotension - Hypoxemia - Ileus - Nausea or vomiting - Tachycardia - Tachypnea • Measurement of either serum lipase (CPT code 83690) or amylase (CPT code 82150) concentration IS NOT REIMBURSABLE more than once per week. • Measurement of serum amylase (CPT code 82150) concentration IS NOT REIMBURSABLE when billed in conjunction with serum lipase concentration (CPT code 83690). • Measurement of either serum lipase (CPT code 83690) or amylase (CPT code 82150) concentration IS NOT REIMBURSABLE in any of the following situations: - For all other situations or conditions not described above - For asymptomatic individuals during a general exam without abnormal findings - For individuals with a diagnosis of chronic pancreatitis • Measurement of serum or urine trypsin, trypsinogen or trypsinogen activation peptide (TAP) (CPT code 83519) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE in any of the following situations: - For asymptomatic individuals during a general exam without abnormal findings - For individuals with a diagnosis of acute pancreatitis • Measurement of the following biomarkers with a diagnosis of acute pancreatitis IS NOT REIMBURSABLE : - C-reactive protein (CRP) (CPT code 86140, CPT code 86141) - Interleukin-6 (IL-6) (CPT code 83529) - Interleukin-8 (IL-8) (CPT code 83520) - Procalcitonin (CPT code 84145) Applicable procedures for Medicare Advantage plans

rule_statement: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Serum intact parathyroid (PTH) testing (CPT code 83970*) IS REIMBURSABLE for individuals with any of the following conditions at the designated frequency: - As needed for individuals who have: • The following signs of hypoparathyroidism: - Abnormal magnesium - Elevated serum phosphorus - Hypercalciuria - Hypocalcemia - Low calcitriol • Abnormal calcium • Familial medullary thyroid carcinoma • Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A • Osteoporosis or low bone mass • Undergone parathyroidectomy - One test per year for individuals who have been diagnosed with hyperparathyroidism but who have not undergone parathyroidectomy - One test every 12 months for individuals who have been diagnosed with stage 3 chronic kidney disease (CKD) - One test every three months for individuals who have been diagnosed with stage 4 or stage 5 CKD - One test every three months for individuals who are younger than 18 years of age and who have been diagnosed with pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1A or type 1B, pseudopseudohypoparathyroidism, progressive osseous heteroplasia or acrodysostosis - One test per year for individuals who are 18 years of age or older and who have been diagnosed with pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1A or type 1B, pseudopseudohypoparathyroidism, progressive osseous heteroplasia or acrodysostosis Policy Number : LAB2023049 • The following tests ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE for individuals with a primary diagnosis representing a general encounter without abnormal findings: - Serum, blood or fecal magnesium testing (CPT code 83735**) - Serum ionized calcium (CPT code 82330) or urine calcium testing (CPT code 82340) - Urine phosphorus or phosphate testing (CPT code 84105) Applicable procedures for Medicare Advantage plans

policy_title: Laboratory - Testing for Diagnosis of Active or Latent Tuberculosis
rule_statement: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • An interferon gamma release assay (IGRA) (CPT code 86480, CPT code 86481) and an acid fast bacilli (AFB) smear or stain (CPT code 87116) ARE REIMBURSABLE to diagnose latent tuberculosis (TB) infection for individuals at risk for infection based on clinical presentation or risk factors noted below upon screening evaluation: • Abnormal weight loss • Acute kidney failure or chronic renal disease • Cough • Crohn's disease • Diabetes mellitus • Enlarged lymph nodes • Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) disease • Immunodeficiency • Lymphoma, leukemia or multiple myeloma • Malignant neoplasm of head, face and neck • Nonspecific reaction to cell mediated immunity measurement of gamma interferon antigen response • Nonspecific reaction to tuberculin skin test without active tuberculosis • Opioid or illicit substance use • Pericardial effusion • Pleural effusion • Pulmonary nodule • Rheumatoid arthritis • Steroid or immunosuppressant use • Transplanted organ and tissue status when screening is mandated • For individuals diagnosed with TB, nucleic acid testing for Mycobacterium (CPT code 87551, CPT code 87556, CPT code 87561) IS REIMBURSABLE. • For individuals with active tuberculosis, IGRA (CPT code 86480, CPT code 86481) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Quantitative nucleic acid testing for Mycobacterium species (CPT code 87552), M. tuberculosis (CPT code 87557) and M. avium complex (CPT code 87562) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Genotyping of Mycobacterium species (CPT code 87150, CPT code 87153) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Adenosine deaminase (ADA) (CPT code 84311) levels in cerebrospinal, pleural, peritoneal, pericardial and other fluids for the diagnosis of extrapulmonary TB IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Tests designed to detect or diagnose TB through detection of serum biomarkers (CPT code 0574U) ARE NOT REIMBURSABLE.

policy_title: Laboratory - Venous and Arterial Thrombosis Testing
rule_statement: As a Medicare Advantage plan, we have developed payment policies to explain coverage more fully for services. The criteria outlined will apply to Medicare Advantage plans except when the procedure(s) has established criteria through the Original Medicare National Coverage Determinations (NCDs) and Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs) as outlined below. In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. • Plasma testing for protein C deficiency (CPT code 85302, CPT code 85303), protein S deficiency (CPT code 85305, CPT code 85306) and antithrombin III deficiency (CPT code 85300, CPT code 85301) IS REIMBURSABLE for any of the following situations: - Acute coronary syndromes including myocardial infarction - Any deep venous thrombosis - Arterial ischemic stroke - Deep phlebothrombosis in pregnancy - Disseminated intravascular coagulation, also known as defibrination syndrome - Pulmonary embolism - Relatives of individuals with deep venous thrombosis • Plasma testing for protein C deficiency (CPT code 85302, CPT code 85303) or protein S deficiency (CPT code 85305, CPT code 85306) IS REIMBURSABLE for any of the following situations: - Neonatal purpura fulminans - Warfarin-induced skin necrosis • Venous thrombosis risk testing (CPT codes 85300-85303, CPT code 85305, CPT code 85306) for superficial venous thrombosis, including superficial thrombophlebitis and varicosities, IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • The activated protein C resistance assay (CPT code 85307) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . • Multi-gene panel testing (CPT code 0278U*) IS NOT REIMBURSABLE . rule_statement: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) allows some physicians and practitioners to opt out of the Medicare Program for a period of two years. At the end of two years, a provider can opt in to the Medicare Program, or continue to opt out for another two-year period. Providers should refer to CMS and relevant Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) publications to understand the formal opt-out process. Providers who opt out of the Medicare Program agree to the following conditions during their opt-out period: • A provider and a Medicare beneficiary, including a Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plan member, must enter into a private contract for services that the Medicare Program would otherwise cover. Limitations on charges imposed by the Medicare Program are not applicable to services furnished by opt-out providers under a private contract. Therefore, the beneficiary agrees to pay for all services furnished by the opt-out provider based on the terms of their private contract. • A provider must not request payment from the Medicare Program during the opt-out period. - Exception: Providers can request payment from the Medicare Program for emergency or urgently needed services when no private contract exists between the beneficiary and the opt-out provider. Providers are required to submit the claim to the Medicare Program on behalf of the beneficiary for emergency or urgently needed services when no private contract exists between the beneficiary and the opt-out provider. Limitations on charges imposed by the Medicare Program are applicable for emergency or urgently needed services. • A provider must not contract with a Medicare beneficiary at the time the beneficiary is seeking emergency or urgently needed services.

rule_statement: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans recognize that a provider can charge a patient for a missed appointment, as long as the provider applies their policy according to the standards outlined in Chapter 1, Section 30.3.13 of the Medicare Claims Processing Manual. Therefore, a provider must apply any policy regarding a missed appointment equally to all patients, whether they are enrolled in the Medicare Program or not. A missed appointment fee must be the same for Medicare beneficiaries and patients who are not Medicare beneficiaries. The fee is not a charge for a health care service but compensates the provider for a missed business opportunity. A hospital may charge a patient for a missed appointment in the hospital's outpatient department only if the patient is not receiving inpatient services at the time of the missed appointment. The hospital would violate 42 CFR 489.22 if it were to charge a registered hospital inpatient a fee for missing an appointment in the hospital's outpatient department. Consistent with Original Medicare, Humana MA plans do not reimburse for a missed appointment charge imposed by a provider. A missed appointment fee should not be billed to Humana. If a provider submits a charge to Humana for a missed appointment fee, Humana will deny the charge, indicating the service is not covered under the patient's MA plan.
trigger_conditions: if the patient is not receiving inpatient services at the time of the missed appointment

The following applies to professional services only. Modifier 22 may be added to a procedure code to indicate that the work required to provide a service was substantially greater than is typically required. Documentation must support the substantial additional work and the reason for the additional work. Examples of circumstances that might require substantial additional work for which it is appropriate to report modifier 22 include increased intensity, time or technical difficulty of the service; increased severity of the patient's condition; and increased physical or mental effort required to provide the service. Additional service time alone does not justify the use of modifier 22 . Modifier 22 should be reported only with a procedure code that has a global surgery period of 0, 10 or 90 days. Modifier 22 should not be appended to an evaluation and management (E/M) service. Humana determines additional reimbursement, if any, for a procedure code submitted with modifier 22 , based on individual consideration of unusual circumstances as documented in the medical record or operative report. Humana does not allow more than the billed charge amount for a procedure code submitted with modifier 22 .

rule_statement: Bilateral procedures are procedures that are performed on similar sites on opposite sides of the body, during the same session, by the same qualified health care practitioner. When a procedure reported using a service code with a Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File (RVF) bilateral indicator 1 is performed bilaterally, providers must report the code with either modifier 50 or with anatomical modifiers such as modifiers LT and RT . Humana strongly encourages providers to report a bilateral procedure using modifier 50 rather than modifiers LT and RT , but accepts both methods. When using modifier 50 to report a bilateral procedure, report a single claim line with a unit of 1. When using modifiers LT and RT to report a bilateral procedure, report two claim lines, each with a unit of 1. Only report modifier 50 when the procedure is performed on similar but opposite sites. For example, report modifier 50 for the same service code for a procedure performed on the right and left knee. However, do not report modifier 50 for the same service code for a procedure performed on the right knee and left shoulder. When reporting two or more bilateral procedures using the same code, report the first bilateral procedure on a single claim line with a unit of 1 using modifier 50 and report a single claim line with a unit of 1 for all subsequent bilateral procedures using modifier 50 and modifier 59. It is not necessary to report modifier 50 with a service code with an MPFS RVF bilateral indicator other than 1.

rule_statement: Humana only applies a bilateral payment adjustment to procedures reported using a service code with a MPFS RVF bilateral indicator 1. When a bilateral payment adjustment applies, the amount allowed for a bilaterally performed procedure is the lesser of the following: • The total charged for both sides; or • 150 percent of either - the provider's contracted rate that would have applied if the procedure had been done unilaterally or - the base maximum amount payable under the member's plan , for an out-of-network provider, that would have applied if the procedure had been done unilaterally. A single claim line with an MPFS RVF bilateral indicator 1 code billed with modifier 50 is processed as one unit. Providers may submit supporting documentation for reconsideration of additional units. In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply. For example, when a bilaterally performed procedure is reported with another procedure for the same date of service, a multiple procedure payment reduction may be applied after the bilateral payment

rule_statement: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. This policy applies only to charges for practitioner services for procedure codes identified, in the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value file , as having global surgery periods. Humana plans consider a return trip to the operating or procedure room, as indicated by the use of modifier 78 , as surgical only and allow the appropriate rate for the service, which is the practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan , multiplied by the MPFS intraoperative percentage. For a charge for an unlisted code submitted with modifier 78 , Humana plans allow 50 percent of the intraoperative amount of the original surgical procedure that resulted in the return to the operating or procedure room. Multiple surgery and bilateral rules do not apply on return trips to the operating or procedure room. Reimbursement for modifier 78 charges for assistant at surgery services is not subject to multiplication by the intraoperative percentage. It is inappropriate to bill modifiers 76, 77 or 79 with modifier 78 ; therefore, Humana plans deny a charge submitted with modifier 78 and any of those modifiers.

rule_statement: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has directed providers to use modifier CT to report computed tomography (CT) services furnished on equipment that is not consistent with dose optimization standards established by the National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA). Enforcement of NEMA Standard XR 29-2013, also known as the MITA Smart Dose standard, for the Medicare Program is required by the Protecting Access to Medicare Act of 2014. The criteria of NEMA Standard XR 29-2013 ensure use of the lowest radiation dose necessary to get the image quality needed by providers to make a proper diagnosis. The standard outlines four attributes CT equipment should meet to ensure that a patient receives the highest standard of care as established by professional societies and regulatory agencies. Performing CT services on equipment that meets all elements of the standard helps reduce a patient's lifetime exposure to potentially cancer-causing medical radiation. Humana works to reduce our members' exposure to medical radiation. Directly and through vendor partnerships, we educate our members on the risks of medical radiation exposure and encourage our in-network providers to provide high quality advanced diagnostic services that meet a broad set of industry standards, including NEMA Standard XR 29-2013. This policy outlines Humana's billing requirements and reimbursement for services reported with modifier CT .
trigger_conditions: Applicable to Modifier CT services under Medicare Advantage.

rule_statement: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) has directed providers to use modifier FX to report X-ray services furnished using film. Effective for dates of service beginning January 1, 2017, Original Medicare reimbursement for the technical component (TC) of film X-ray services reported with modifier FX is reduced by 20 percent. The film X-ray reimbursement reduction is required for the Medicare Program by the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2016. Transitioning from film X-ray technology to digital radiography (DR) technology ensures use of the lowest radiation dose necessary to get the image quality needed by providers to make a proper diagnosis. Performing X-rays using DR technology ensures that a patient receives the highest standard of care as established by professional societies and regulatory agencies and helps reduce a patient's lifetime exposure to potentially cancer-causing medical radiation. Humana works to reduce our members' exposure to medical radiation. Directly and through vendor partnerships, we educate our members on the risks of medical radiation exposure and encourage our in-network providers to provide high quality advanced diagnostic services that meet a broad set of industry standards.
trigger_conditions: Applicable to Modifier FX services under Medicare Advantage.
exceptions_overrides: Standard payer clinical claim editing rules apply; no automated bypass.

rule_statement: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) global surgical policy states that reimbursement for a procedure that has a global surgical package includes payment for preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative care, as well as payment for various related services, such as complications following surgery, postsurgical pain management and supplies. There are occasions when more than one qualified healthcare practitioner provides services included in the global surgical package of a surgery. For example, the physician who performs the surgical procedure may not provide the follow-up care. In situations in which, for a global surgical package that may be split, there is an agreed transfer of care, it is appropriate to reimburse the various practitioners for portions of the global surgical package . For a surgery with a global surgical package , a qualified healthcare practitioner indicates the portion of the global surgical package performed by using modifiers 54, 55 and 56 , as appropriate. This policy outlines Humana's reimbursement for a service reported with modifier 54, 55 or 56 .
trigger_conditions: when more than one qualified healthcare practitioner provides services included in the global surgical package of a surgery

rule_statement: In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. This policy applies to global surgery procedure codes as identified on the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File and applies only to charges for practitioner services. Humana plans determine the amount allowed for a segment of split global care for a service with a global surgery period as outlined below. Humana allows a charge for preoperative management only, indicated by modifier 56 , at the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for the service multiplied by that service's MPFS preoperative percentage. Humana allows a charge for intraoperative care only, indicated by modifier 54 , at the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for the service multiplied by that service's MPFS intraoperative percentage. Humana allows a charge for postoperative management only, as indicated by modifier 55 , at the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for the service, multiplied by that service's MPFS postoperative percentage, and multiplied by the percentage of the global surgery period for which the billing practitioner provided care. Effectively, the total of all percentages of a global surgery period for which practitioners were responsible for postoperative management is 100%. Therefore, the plan does not allow more than 100% of the postoperative management for that service. Humana expects a practitioner to report, in the units field on the claim form, the number of days of service that the practitioner provided, consistent with the transfer of postoperative management to which the practitioners agreed. However, if a Medicare A/B MAC directs providers to report the number of days differently, Humana MA plans permit out-of-network providers in the jurisdiction to report days consistent with the MAC 's guidance. Humana considers a charge submitted with modifier 54 as a charge for both preoperative management and intraoperative care , unless there is a coverable charge for the same procedure code for preoperative management only, as indicated by modifier 56 . If there is a coverable charge submitted with modifier 56 for the same service, the plan considers a charge submitted with modifier 54 as a charge for intraoperative care only.

rule_statement: • Base maximum amount payable under the member's plan : The maximum amount of reimbursement for a covered expense, determined by the member's plan. Depending on the plan, this may be the maximum allowable fee, the appropriate Medicare fee schedule rate or an amount derived from another payment model. Actual plan reimbursement may be less than this base maximum amount, because of applicable adjustments. • Global surgery period(s) : The number of days that constitute preoperative management, intraoperative care and postoperative management. - Zero-day minor surgery or procedure: Day of surgery only for a total global period of one day. - 10-day minor surgery or procedure: Zero preoperative management days, day of surgery and 10 postoperative management days for a total global period of 11 days. - 90-day major surgery or procedure: One preoperative management day, day of surgery and 90 postoperative management days for a total global period of 92 days. • Global surgical package : All services for which reimbursement would be included in a global surgery payment; services that would be separately reimbursable are not part of the global surgical package. • Intraoperative care : For a service with a global surgery period, the surgical care, including postoperative care before discharge from the hospital. • MAC : Medicare Administrative Contractor. • Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File : A file published by CMS that includes, among other information, percentages of the global surgical package for the preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative management of a patient; and the professional procedure relative value unit (RVU). • Modifier 54 : Surgical care only. • Modifier 55 : Postoperative management only. • Modifier 56 : Preoperative management only. • Preoperative management : For a service with a global surgery period, that portion of a global surgical package provided before the surgical care. • Postoperative management : For a service with a global surgery period, that portion of a global surgical package provided after the surgical care and after discharge from the hospital. • Split global care : Global surgical package services provided, under a transfer of care, by multiple qualified healthcare practitioners.
trigger_conditions: Applicable to Modifiers 54, 55 and 56 services under Medicare Advantage.
