rule_statement: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana expects each healthcare provider to administer drugs and biologicals, collectively referred to as drugs, efficiently and in a clinically appropriate manner. This includes using multi-dose vials or packages when available and clinically appropriate. Humana also expects providers to use the combination of available single-dose vials or packages that results in the least amount of discarded drug. For example, if: • A drug is only available in single-dose 500 milligram and 120 milligram vials, • 540 milligrams are administered, and • The Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) code defines one base unit of the code as 10 milligrams, Then five of the 120 milligram vials should be used, resulting in a discarded amount of 60 milligrams (6 units). It is not appropriate to use a combination of one 500 milligram vial and one 120 milligram vial, resulting in a discarded amount of 80 milligrams (8 units). Humana reimburses for the discarded amount of a drug when all of the following criteria are satisfied: • The drug is a covered expense, • The discarded amount is the remainder of a single-dose vial or package used to treat the patient, and • The drug is billed as described below. When those criteria are satisfied, Humana reimburses no more, for the total administered and total discarded, for a drug than the amount appropriate, in dollars, for the efficient administration amount of the drug.
trigger_conditions: when available and clinically appropriate

rule_statement: When there is a discarded amount of drug from a single-dose vial or package, Humana expects providers to report modifier JW according to applicable Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidance. When, as discussed above, a discarded amount is reimbursable for a date of service, the billing provider must submit two lines, as described below, using the HCPCS code appropriate for that drug for that date of service: The number of base units submitted for each of the two lines must be calculated using the appropriate unit size indicated by the HCPCS code description. The first of the two lines must indicate the number of base units appropriate for the amount administered to the patient, with fractions rounded up to the next highest whole number of base units . For example, if: • 14 milligrams are administered and • The HCPCS code defines one base unit of the code as 10 milligrams, Then the first of the two lines must indicate 2 units of the HCPCS code because the 14 milligrams administered are one base unit of the HCPCS code and a fraction of a second base unit of the HCPCS code. The second of the two lines, with modifier JW appended, must indicate the number of base units that is the difference between the efficient administration amount and the number of base units indicated on the first of the two lines. Continuing the example above, if: • 14 milligrams are administered, • The HCPCS code defines one base unit of the code as 10 milligrams, and • Of the vials available for provider purchase, the amount that results in the least amount of discarded drug is one 30 milligram vial Then the second of the two lines must indicate 1 unit of the HCPCS code because • The efficient administration amount is 30 milligrams, • The number of base units for the efficient administration amount is 3, and • The difference between the number of base units for the efficient administration amount (3) and the number of base units indicated on the first of the two lines (2) is 1. For each of those two lines, the provider must submit a charge amount that is the charge amount applicable per base unit multiplied by the number of base units indicated for that line. Continuing the example above: For each drug with a reimbursable discarded amount for a date of service, the combined amount charged for both lines must not exceed the total charge that would be appropriate if, for the efficient administration amount , the provider had administered all of each vial or package used. If the number of base units that would be appropriate for the billing of the first of two lines equals the number of base units for the efficient administration amount , then, instead of submitting two lines, the provider submits only one line with modifier JZ . For example, if: • 40 milligrams are administered, • The HCPCS code defines one base unit of the code as 25 milligrams, and • Of the vials available for provider purchase, the amount that results in the least amount of discarded drug is two 25 milligram vials, Then only one line is submitted and must indicate 2 units of the HCPCS code because the 40 milligrams administered are one base unit of the HCPCS code and a fraction of a second base unit of the HCPCS code. Suppliers who dispense but do not administer drugs from single-dose vials and packages should report modifier JW when there was a discarded amount of drug during the preparation process before supplying the drug. rule_statement: This policy outlines various multiple procedure payment reductions (MPPR). Practitioner reimbursement for a procedure code generally includes reimbursement for the individual costs, also known as inputs, typically associated with that service. For example, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) uses a formula that accounts for the inputs associated with a procedure code to determine Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) reimbursement rates for that code. When the same provider renders multiple services, or multiple units of the same service, to the same patient on the same day, the total calculation for the procedure code(s) could account more than once for an input that was only rendered once. Examples of inputs that might be contemplated in reimbursement for certain procedure codes, that would not typically be duplicated in the same encounter include: greeting and gowning the patient; preparing the room, equipment and supplies; providing education and obtaining consent. An MPPR adjusts reimbursement to offset duplication of reimbursement for inputs that were only rendered once.
trigger_conditions: When the same provider renders multiple services, or multiple units of the same service, to the same patient on the same day, the total calculation for the procedure code(s) could account more than once for an input that was only rendered once

rule_statement: For diagnostic cardiovascular services, the portion of an in-network practitioner's contracted rate that is attributable to the technical component (TC) may be subject to MPPR. For diagnostic cardiovascular services rendered by an out-of-network practitioner, the portion of the base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to the TC may be subject to MPPR. For reimbursement of only a TC , all of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan is attributable to the TC . For reimbursement of both a TC and a professional component (PC) , the portion of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to the TC is that rate or amount multiplied by the ratio of the code's MPFS local TC amount to the code's MPFS local global amount. For example: MMMMMMMM llllllllll TTTT aaaaaaaaaaaa MMMMMMMM llllllllll gggggggggggg aaaaaaaaaaaa Humana applies an MPPR to same-day diagnostic cardiovascular TC services rendered by the same provider . rule_statement: Diagnostic Imaging Services Technical Component For diagnostic imaging services, the portion of an in-network practitioner's contracted rate that is attributable to the TC may be subject to MPPR. For diagnostic imaging services rendered by an out-of-network practitioner, the portion of the base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to the TC may be subject to MPPR. For reimbursement of only a TC , all of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan is attributable to the TC . For reimbursement of both a TC and a PC , the portion of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to the TC is that rate or amount multiplied by the ratio of the code's MPFS local TC amount to the code's MPFS local global amount. Humana applies an MPPR to same-day diagnostic imaging TC services rendered by the same provider . To determine whether the MPPR applies to a specific allowed charge or to one or more units of a charge with multiple allowed units: First, of the services for which Humana is reimbursing for a TC , Humana identifies the same-day services with a MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 4. Second, Humana ranks all identified services from highest dollar amount to lowest dollar amount. We rank by the portion of the charge's per-unit practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to TC , as described above. Finally, Humana eliminates from review the unit of service that is ranked highest; or, if multiple units of service are ranked highest, Humana eliminates one of those units. Humana applies MPPR to all other allowed units of service. When Humana determines to apply diagnostic imaging services TC MPPR to a unit, a 50 percent reduction is applied to the reimbursement for the portion of the unit's practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to TC . Note: In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply. Diagnostic Imaging Professional Component For diagnostic imaging services, the portion of an in-network practitioner's contracted rate that is attributable to the PC may be subject to MPPR. For diagnostic imaging services rendered by an out-of-network practitioner, the portion of the base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to the PC may be subject to MPPR. For reimbursement of only a PC , all of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan is attributable to the PC . For reimbursement of both a PC and a TC , the portion of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to the PC is that rate or amount multiplied by the ratio of the code's MPFS local PC amount to the code's MPFS local global amount. Humana applies an MPPR to same-day diagnostic imaging PC services rendered by the same provider . To determine whether the MPPR applies to a specific allowed charge or to one or more units of a charge with multiple allowed units: First, of the services for which Humana is reimbursing for a PC , Humana identifies the same-day services with a MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 4. Second, Humana ranks all identified services from highest dollar amount to lowest dollar amount. We rank by the portion of the charge's per-unit practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to PC , as described above. Finally, Humana eliminates from review the unit of service that is ranked highest; or, if multiple units of service are ranked highest, Humana eliminates one of those units. Humana applies MPPR to all other allowed units of service. When Humana determines to apply diagnostic imaging services PC MPPR to a unit: • For dates of service on or after January 1, 2017, a 5 percent reduction is applied to the reimbursement for the portion of the unit's practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to PC . • For dates of service before January 1, 2017, a 25 percent reduction is applied to the reimbursement for the portion of the unit's practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to PC . Note: In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply. Diagnostic Imaging Technical and Professional Component Any charge could be subject to a TC MPPR, PC MPPR or both. When both TC MPPR and PC MPPR are applied, calculation of the TC MPPR is separate from calculation of the PC MPPR. The rankings of TC and PC are independent of each other. For example: First, of the services for which Humana is reimbursing for a TC and PC , Humana identifies the same-day services with a MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 4. Second, Humana ranks all identified services from highest dollar amount to lowest dollar amount. We rank by the portion of the charge's per-unit practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to TC and PC separately, as described above. Finally, Humana eliminates from review the unit of service that is ranked highest for TC and PC separately. Humana applies TC MPPR and PC MPPR separately to all other allowed units of service. When Humana determines to apply diagnostic imaging services TC MPPR to a unit, a 50 percent reduction is applied to the reimbursement for the portion of the unit's practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to TC . When Humana determines to apply diagnostic imaging services PC MPPR to a unit, for dates of service on or after January 1, 2017, a 5 percent reduction is applied to the reimbursement for the portion of the unit's practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to PC .

rule_statement: For diagnostic ophthalmology services, the portion of an in-network practitioner's contracted rate that is attributable to the TC may be subject to MPPR. For diagnostic ophthalmology services rendered by an out-of-network practitioner, the portion of the base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to the TC may be subject to MPPR. For reimbursement of only a TC , all of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan is attributable to the TC . For reimbursement of both a TC and a PC , the portion of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to the TC is that rate or amount multiplied by the ratio of the code's MPFS local TC amount to the code's MPFS local global amount. For example: MMMMMMMM llllllllll TTTT aaaaaaaaaaaa MMMMMMMM llllllllll gggggggggggg aaaaaaaaaaaa Humana applies an MPPR to same-day diagnostic ophthalmology TC services rendered by the same provider . To determine whether the MPPR applies to a specific allowed charge or to one or more units of a charge with multiple allowed units: First, of the services for which Humana is reimbursing for a TC , Humana identifies the same-day services with a MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 7. Second, Humana ranks all identified services from highest dollar amount to lowest dollar amount. We rank by the portion of the charge's per-unit practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to TC , as described above. Finally, Humana eliminates from review the unit of service that is ranked highest; or, if multiple units of service are ranked highest, Humana eliminates one of those units. Humana applies MPPR to all other allowed units of service. When Humana determines to apply diagnostic ophthalmology services TC MPPR to a unit, a 20 percent reduction is applied to the reimbursement for the portion of the unit's practitioner's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan that is attributable to TC . Note: In certain circumstances, additional payment rules may apply.

rule_statement: For endoscopic services rendered by an in-network practitioner, the contracted rate may be subject to MPPR. For endoscopic services rendered by an out-of-network practitioner, the base maximum amount payable under the member's plan may be subject to MPPR. Humana applies an MPPR to same-family endoscopic procedures, including multiple units of the same procedure code, rendered by the same provider on the same day. To determine whether the MPPR applies to a specific allowed charge: First, of the services for which Humana is reimbursing, Humana identifies, for a date of service, all MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 3 endoscopy codes and identifies each service's base endoscopy code. Second, Humana groups all services with the same endoscopy base code. Each group of services with the same base code is one endoscopic family. Third, when there are multiple procedure codes for an endoscopic family and one of those is the family's base code, Humana denies separate reimbursement for that base code charge. Reimbursement for the base code is included in reimbursement for the highest ranked procedure code in that endoscopic family. Humana ranks all reimbursable services within each endoscopic family by the procedure's contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan . Finally, within each endoscopic family, Humana reduces reimbursement for each procedure code, except that family's highest ranked procedure. The amount Humana uses to reduce reimbursement for a procedure code is the amount allowed for the procedure's base code. When a contracted rate does not include an amount allowed for a base code, Humana will apply the following formula based on amounts provided by CMS. These amounts are used to create a reduction amount. The reduction amount is then applied to the contracted rate. Endoscopic procedures are also subject to multiple surgery reduction. As discussed in the Multiple Surgery section below, each endoscopic family is treated as a single surgery for determination of a multiple surgery reduction. information.
trigger_conditions: when there are multiple procedure codes for an endoscopic family and one of those is the family's base code, Humana denies separate reimbursement for that base code charge
exceptions_overrides: except that family's highest ranked procedure

rule_statement: Humana applies a multiple surgery reduction when: • The same provider performs more than one same-day MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 2 service; or • The same provider performs endoscopic procedures in more than one endoscopic family on the same day (see Multiple Endoscopic Procedures section above); or • The same provider performs at least one MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 2 service and at least one endoscopic procedure on the same day. In unique circumstances, for the purposes of applying a multiple surgery reduction: • Humana may not consider an MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator 2 service as a surgery. • Humana may consider a service that does not have an MPFS Relative Value File multiple procedure indicator of 2 as a surgery. Multiple surgery reduction applies to same-day services whether or not those services were submitted with modifier 51 , modifier 59 or modifiers X{EPSU}. Humana plans apply a multiple surgery reduction as follows: • The procedure with the highest contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan is not reduced; and • All other procedures are reduced by 50 percent. Special Rules for Endoscopic Services For an endoscopic service, multiple endoscopy reduction and multiple surgery reduction are determined separately. This will result in one of the following scenarios, depending on the number of services billed and the individual multiple procedure indicator code of each service : • Multiple endoscopy reduction alone could apply to the service. • Multiple surgery reduction alone could apply to the service. • Both multiple endoscopy reduction and multiple surgery reduction could apply to the service. • Neither multiple endoscopy reduction nor multiple surgery reduction could apply to the service. If multiple endoscopy reduction applies, it is always determined before multiple surgery reduction. After determining any multiple endoscopy reductions, all endoscopic services in the same endoscopic family are treated as a single service for the purpose of determining multiple surgery reduction, as follows: • For multiple surgery reduction ranking purposes, endoscopic procedures in the same endoscopic family are treated as one service. • An endoscopic family's multiple surgery reduction ranking establishes the multiple surgery reduction percentage, if any, for all services in that endoscopic family. Note : Additional payment rules may apply in certain circumstances. For example, when a bilateral adjustment is applicable, it will be applied before a multiple surgery reduction.
trigger_conditions: If multiple endoscopy reduction applies, it is always determined before multiple surgery reduction

rule_statement: • Always Therapy: A service that is always considered a therapy, as noted in the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File by a multiple procedure indicator 5. • Base maximum amount payable under the member's plan: The maximum amount of reimbursement for a unit of a covered expense, determined by the member's plan. Depending on the plan, this may be the maximum allowable fee, the appropriate Medicare fee schedule rate or an amount derived from another payment model. Actual plan reimbursement may be less than this base maximum amount, because of applicable adjustments. • Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File: A file published by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services that includes, among other information, multiple procedure indicator, relative value units and conversion factors for practitioner services. This file is commonly referred to as the relative value unit (RVU) table. Elements of the file that are referenced in this policy include the following: - CF: The conversion factor is the amount shown in the MPFS Relative Value File for the appropriate year. - PE GPCI: The practice expense geographic price index for the area where the service was rendered, shown in the MPFS Relative Value File for the appropriate year. - PE RVU: The practice expense relative value unit is the amount shown in the MPFS Relative Value File for the appropriate year. • Modifier 26: Professional component. • Modifier 51: Multiple procedures. • Modifier 59: Distinct procedural service. • Modifier TC: Technical component. • Modifiers X{EPSU}: Modifiers XE, XP, XS and XU, collectively. - Modifier XE : Separate encounter. - Modifier XP : Separate practitioner. - Modifier XS : Separate structure. - Modifier XU : Unusual non-overlapping service. • Practice Expense (PE): One of three groups of inputs used to determine pricing of services covered under the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS); PE accounts for costs of running a practice (other than expenses associated with professional liability and the practitioner's actual work), including rent, equipment, supplies and staff costs other than the work performed by the practitioner personally. • Professional Component (PC): The professional component of a service is for practitioner work interpreting a diagnostic test or performing a procedure and includes indirect practice and malpractice expenses related to that work. • Same Provider: A single qualified practitioner or multiple practitioners within the same group practice. • Technical Component (TC): The technical component of a service is for all non-practitioner work and includes administrative, personnel and capital (equipment and facility) costs and related malpractice expenses.

rule_statement: The billing of facility observation services is appropriate only when the observation services were medically necessary, the observation services were ordered by a qualified healthcare professional , the patient was under the care of a physician or qualified nonphysician practitioner during observation services, and one or more of the following is true of the encounter: • Treatment and monitoring were provided to determine if inpatient admission was needed • The observation services were provided for patient monitoring, after outpatient surgery or diagnostic testing, that was beyond the standard recovery period for the service • A qualified healthcare professional directly referred the patient to the facility for observation services • The patient was a child who was observed because of an uncertain clinical response to outpatient therapy • The patient was a child whose parent or caregiver was unavailable or unknown If none of those events occurred, a Humana plan does not reimburse for a facility observation charge. The billing of and reimbursement for observation services are limited to rendered observation services that were specifically medically necessary and typically do not exceed 48 hours. Any time for any of the following scenarios is excluded from the calculation of billable observation hours: • Patient monitoring during diagnostic or therapeutic services, including observation care interrupted by such services • Routine preparation for outpatient surgery and diagnostic testing • Services provided during the standard recovery period after outpatient surgery, which is four to six hours, or after diagnostic testing • Services provided for the convenience of the patient, physician or qualified nonphysician practitioner • Observation services provided according to a standing order • The time period between the order for observation services and when observation services began • The time period between observation services ending and the patient's discharge • The time period between observation services ending and the arrival of the patient's transportation

rule_statement: services. Routine items, supplies and services already included in other outpatient charges are not separately billable. Medicare Advantage Payment Policy Medicare Advantage Payment Policy In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. This policy applies to outpatient facilities that include, but are not limited to, hospital outpatient departments and ambulatory surgery centers. To separately bill for items, supplies and services, a provider must consistently follow its customary charging practices for all Medicare and non-Medicare patients, for all payers and health plans. Humana sometimes reviews an itemized bill for an outpatient encounter to determine whether supplies, items and services specified on the itemized bill are separately billable. The following supplies, items and services are typically not separately billable and, therefore, not separately payable from primary service charge(s). Please note that the examples given do not represent an exhaustive list. • Any supplies, items and services that, under customary charging practices , are included in charges for a specific service or in charges for the delivery of services in a specific location. Examples of included supplies and services are bandages, IV flushing, dressing changes, equipment monitoring and routine nursing care and assessments. • All items and supplies that may be purchased over the counter, such as personal care items, ice packs, alcohol wipes and cotton balls. • All reusable items, supplies and equipment that are provided to all patients on a routine basis during an outpatient encounter; this applies to all outpatient encounters. Examples of reusable items, supplies and equipment are cardiac monitors and durable medical equipment (DME) items used while in an outpatient facility.

rule_statement: Note: This section does not apply to clinical diagnostic laboratory tests paid by Original Medicare under the Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule. A physician or other professional may bill for the technical component (TC) and/or professional component (PC) of a diagnostic test that was ordered by the physician or other professional, or ordered by a party related to the billing physician or other supplier through common ownership or control. However, anti-markup payment limitations apply if the diagnostic test is performed by a physician who does not "share a practice" with the billing physician or other professional. The performing provider for the TC is the professional who conducted or supervised the test, and the performing provider for the PC is the professional who interpreted the results. Under anti-markup payment limitations, payment to the billing physician or other professional, minus beneficiary cost-sharing, for the TC or PC of the diagnostic test may not exceed the lowest of the following amounts: • The performing provider's net charge, excluding any charges for equipment or space leased, to the billing physician or other professional; • The billing physician's or other professional's actual charge; and • The amount for the test that would be allowed if the performing provider billed directly.
trigger_conditions: if the diagnostic test is performed by a physician who does not "share a practice" with the billing physician or other professional
exceptions_overrides: Standard payer clinical claim editing rules apply; no automated bypass.

rule_statement: If the performing physician is deemed to "share a practice" with the billing physician or other professional who ordered the test, the anti-markup payment limitation does not apply. A performing physician is considered to "share a practice" with the billing physician or other professional if either: • The performing physician provides "substantially all" (at least 75 percent) of his or her professional services through the billing physician or other professional, as discussed below; or • The services were performed under a "site of service/same building" arrangement as discussed below. The "substantially all" services requirement will be satisfied if, at the time the billing physician or other professional submits a claim for a service provided by the performing physician, the billing physician or other professional has a reasonable belief that: • For the 12 months prior to and including the month in which the service was performed, the performing physician provided substantially all of his or her professional services through the billing physician or other professional; or • The performing physician will provide substantially all of his or her professional services through the billing physician or other professional for the next 12 months (including the month in which the service is performed). The performing physician may be deemed to "share a practice" with the billing physician or other professional if the services were performed under a "site of service/same building" arrangement. This alternative approach requires the performing physician to be an owner, employer or independent contractor of the billing physician or other professional and requires that the TC or PC be performed in the "office of the billing physician or other supplier." The "office of the billing physician or other supplier" is any medical office space, regardless of the number of locations, in which the ordering physician or other professional regularly provides patient care. It also includes space where the billing physician or other supplier furnishes diagnostic testing services, if the space is located in the "same building" in which the ordering physician or other ordering professional regularly provides patient care. With respect to a billing physician or other professional that is a "physician organization," the "office of the billing physician or other supplier" is space in which the ordering physician provides substantially the full range of patient care services the ordering physician provides generally. "Same building" and "physician organization" are defined in 42 CFR §411.351. The billing physician or other professional must keep on file the performing physician's name, address and the National Provider Identifier. The physician or other professional providing the TC or PC of the diagnostic test must be enrolled in the Medicare Program. No formal reassignment is necessary.
trigger_conditions: If the performing physician is deemed to "share a practice" with the billing physician or other professional who ordered the test, the anti-markup payment limitation does not apply

rule_statement: Same-Claim Billing Requirements In the absence of applicable regulatory standards, Humana generally requires providers to submit all charges for the same encounter on one claim. Additionally, Humana generally requires a provider that submits a professional claim to report all charges for same-day services on that claim, regardless of whether they pertain to the same encounter . Exceptions: • When reference laboratory billing is acceptable, Humana permits a reference laboratory reporting charges for testing performed in distinct, specific service facility locations to submit a distinct claim for each service facility location. Note that this exception does not permit a reference laboratory to submit multiple claims for testing, that would otherwise be subject to a general requirement above, for the same service facility location. • Humana permits Tax Equity and Fiscal Responsibility Act (TEFRA) hospital interim claim billing, consistent with Original Medicare's guidance on interim claim billing. Same-Claim Billing Prohibitions Apart from same-day professional-claim services, Humana generally does not permit a provider to report charges for services furnished in multiple encounters on the same claim. However, Humana also permits providers to report charges, on the same outpatient hospital claim, for repetitive services furnished in multiple encounters during the same calendar month.

rule_statement: A colonoscopy allows the physician to examine the lining of the entire large intestine. It is most often used as a screening procedure to look for early signs of cancer in the colon or rectum. However, the test may reveal inflamed tissue, abnormal growths and ulcers. Special instruments can be passed through the colonoscope to remove any polyps if needed. In these cases, the screening colonoscopy results in a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure. This policy describes Humana's billing expectation for distinguishing between a screening colonoscopy and a screening colonoscopy that results in a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure.

rule_statement: Humana does not reimburse, under Medicare Advantage (MA) basic benefits, for self-administered drugs that are given in the outpatient hospital setting in the applicable jurisdiction. Self-administered drugs given in an outpatient hospital setting should be reported on hospital institutional claims using revenue code 0637 and Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) code A9270 . Drugs and biologicals given in an outpatient hospital setting that are not self-administered drugs should be reported using the combination of the applicable revenue code and applicable Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) or HCPCS code. A Humana MA member with Medicare Part D prescription drug coverage may be entitled to coverage of self-administered drugs by the Part D benefit carrier, and the enrollee may request reimbursement from that Part D benefit carrier.

rule_statement: Humana requires a provider to submit a charge for an Original Medicare telehealth service according to the applicable Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidance for the date of service. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans allow Original Medicare telehealth services consistent with the applicable CMS guidance for the date of service. Humana MA plans deny charges for Original Medicare telehealth services that do not satisfy the applicable CMS guidance, including billing guidance regarding the appropriate place of service (POS) code or modifier, for the date of service. For further information on the service codes that may be reported as an Original Medicare telehealth service , see CMS's List of Telehealth Services . Note: Humana MA plans have been applying the Congressionally-authorized, coverage-related waivers to Original Medicare telehealth services . These waivers expire December 31, 2027. Following CMS guidelines, Humana will apply the applicable limitations to a claim for a telehealth service beginning January 1, 2028, unless the service qualifies for coverage under the additional telehealth services benefit. For further information on the limitations that apply to Original Medicare telehealth service beginning January 1, 2028, see the CMS guidance available in the References section of this policy.
trigger_conditions: Applicable to Telehealth and Other Virtual Services services under Medicare Advantage.
exceptions_overrides: unless the service qualifies for coverage under the additional telehealth services benefit

rule_statement: For dates of service beginning January 1, 2020, Humana MA plans also allow certain additional telehealth services that are not Original Medicare telehealth services . Additional telehealth services must meet the following criteria: • The service must be one of those covered under the additional telehealth service benefit in the member's applicable Evidence of Coverage. • The service must be provided by a physician or other qualified healthcare practitioner that has satisfied Humana's telehealth credentialing and recredentialing standards and has a valid and effective contract with Humana. • The service must be provided by a physician or other qualified healthcare practitioner that satisfies the following requirements: - Meets all applicable licensure, certification and registration requirements, including Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) registration, if applicable, in the state(s) in which they practice and the state in which the patient is located at the time of the encounter; - Is operating within the scope of their license; and - Meets professional practice standards in the state(s) in which they practice and the state in which the patient is located at the time of the encounter. • The service must be provided using real-time interactive audio technology, and Humana encourages providers to simultaneously use real-time interactive video technology, when appropriate. For a charge for a particular service to be reimbursed, it must be possible to provide all the necessary components of the code with the real-time interactive technology used. • The physician or other qualified healthcare practitioner must verify the member's identity before providing the service. • The Humana member must provide verbal or written consent to receive the service, in accordance with state law. • The Humana member must be present for the full duration of the service. Services not meeting the criteria outlined above will not be allowed by Humana as additional telehealth services . Unless prohibited by applicable federal statute or regulation, Humana plans allow additional telehealth services if it is medically appropriate to furnish the service via telecommunications-based technology, the service is coverable by the plan, and all applicable coding requirements are satisfied. For further information on the service codes that may be reported as additional telehealth services , see the Medicare Advantage Additional Telehealth Services Benefit Code List section of the policy. Physicians are responsible for supervising any additional telehealth services provided to Humana MA members by nonphysician practitioners within their practices to ensure that such services conform in all respects to the requirements set forth herein. Billing Place of Service Code Humana requires a provider report the POS code for an additional telehealth service as outlined below. For dates of service beginning January 1, 2024, a provider must report one of the following, as appropriate: • POS code 02 • POS code 10 • The applicable hospital POS code, if the patient is at home and the physician or other qualified healthcare practitioner is in the hospital, with modifier 93 or modifier 95 For dates of service from May 12, 2023, through December 31, 2023, a provider must report one of the following, as appropriate: • POS code 02 • POS code 10 • The POS code that would have been reported had the service been furnished in person with modifier 93 • The POS code that would have been reported had the service been furnished in person with modifier 95 Note : The POS code billed for a service will determine whether that service is reimbursed with a facility or nonfacility rate . Audio-Only Modifier Humana requires a provider to identify an audio-only service with modifier 93 . Medicare Advantage Additional Telehealth Services Benefit Code List The attached lists of procedure codes serve as a guide to assist providers in determining which services may be reimbursable under Humana's MA additional telehealth services benefit. Click here* to view the attached code list for the applicable year.
trigger_conditions: if applicable, in the state(s) in which they practice and the state in which the patient is located at the time of the encounter
exceptions_overrides: Unless prohibited by applicable federal statute or regulation, Humana plans allow additional telehealth services if it is medically appropriate to furnish the service via telecommunications-based technology, the service is coverable by the plan, and all applicable coding requirements are satisfied

rule_statement: guidance. Humana MA plans allow such services consistent with the applicable CMS guidance. Humana MA plans deny charges for such services that do not satisfy the applicable CMS guidance. Specific Requirements for Claims Submitted by Federally Qualified Health Centers and Rural Health Clinics A Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) or Rural Health Clinic (RHC) reporting an Original Medicare telehealth service , additional telehealth service , or other virtual service should follow the applicable CMS guidance for the date of service. This also includes, but is not limited to, the following guidance for reporting the correct procedure code for the service: • An Original Medicare telehealth service or additional telehealth service that is a mental health service should be reported with the applicable HCPCS Level II or Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) code for the service rendered. For the service to be allowed as an Original Medicare telehealth service , it must be on CMS's List of Telehealth Services . For the service to be allowed as an additional telehealth service , it must be on the attached list of services that may be reimbursable under Humana's additional telehealth services benefit for the applicable year. • An Original Medicare telehealth service or additional telehealth service that is not a mental health service should be reported with HCPCS code G2025 . • Another virtual service that is covered by Original Medicare but is not an Original Medicare telehealth service , as described above, should be reported according to the applicable CMS guidance for the date of service. For dates of service through December 31, 2025, FQHC and RHC providers should report the virtual service with HCPCS code G0071 . For dates of service beginning January 1, 2026, FQHC and RHC providers should report the virtual service using the same service code as professional providers. In addition, FQHC and RHC providers should append modifier 95 when reporting an Original Medicare telehealth service or additional telehealth service .
trigger_conditions: when reporting an Original Medicare telehealth service or additional telehealth service

To facilitate accurate claims processing of a service that, apart from the active course of treatment exception discussed above, would normally be subject to plan prior authorization requirements, Humana has developed optional modifier or condition codes. Use of these codes may facilitate claims processing by helping Humana identify claims related to an active course of treatment for new members. We encourage each provider to follow the guidance below when submitting claims for services furnished to new enrollees of Humana MA plans other than private fee-for-service (PFFS) plans: • For a professional claim , append modifier TZ to the code reported for each service that was part of an active course of treatment during the 90-day transition period . • For an outpatient facility claim , append modifier TZ to the code reported for each service that was part of an active course of treatment during the 90-day transition period . • For an inpatient facility claim , report condition code 9T for each service that was part of an active course of treatment during the 90-day transition period . A provider must not report the modifier or condition code discussed above to bill for a service: • If the service was not furnished as part of an active course of treatment that began before the member's enrollment in the specific Humana MA plan; or • If the service was not furnished during that enrollment's transition period ; or • If the service was furnished to a member of a Humana MA PFFS plan. In circumstances where a claim for a new member is submitted that may involve an active course of treatment but the provider did not append a modifier or condition code discussed above, Humana may evaluate medical record documentation included with the claim to determine whether the claim involved an active course of treatment . Note: Do not report the modifier or condition code discussed in this policy when submitting claims to Humana commercial or Humana Medicaid plans.

rule_statement: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana may reimburse one charge for professional TCM services per discharge if a patient requires case management when transferring from a facility setting to the community or home setting. Humana requires a provider to follow all TCM requirements as outlined in relevant Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidance. That includes, but is not limited to, the criteria outlined in this policy. Humana reimburses the first TCM charge received for the 30-day service period that meets all of the requirements outlined in this policy. A claim showing discharge from one of the following facility settings must be received to substantiate the necessity of the professional claim for TCM services: • Hospital outpatient observation or partial hospitalization • Inpatient acute care hospital • Inpatient psychiatric hospital • Inpatient rehabilitation facility • Long-term care hospital • Partial hospitalization at a community mental health center • Skilled nursing facility The services associated with the face-to-face portion of the professional TCM service must be rendered by a physician, which is limited to a medical doctor (MD) or doctor of osteopathic medicine (DO), or one of the following nonphysician practitioners (NPPs): nurse practitioner, physician assistant, clinical nurse specialist or certified nurse midwife. This includes behavioral health practitioners such as psychiatrists and psychiatric nurse practitioners. Any portions of the TCM service rendered by clinical staff must be provided under the general supervision of the billing physician or NPP and are subject to applicable state law, scope of practice requirements, and conditions for services and supplies furnished incident to the professional service of a physician or NPP. Clinical staff must meet the requirements of auxiliary personnel as defined by 42 CFR 410.26(a)(1). A qualified health care provider may render TCM services for new or established patients; the reimbursement rate for TCM codes is the same regardless of new or established patient status. Note: Humana plans may reimburse a charge for reasonable and necessary evaluation and management (E/M) services for managing clinical issues, other than E/M services provided on the date of the required TCM face-to-face visit, in addition to a TCM charge, during the 30-day service period. Humana plans do not reimburse: • TCM services rendered by the surgeon during the postoperative period of a 10- or 90-day global surgery. • TCM services when discharge management services are provided by the same provider on the same day. • A TCM charge received after the first allowable TCM, whether from the same or different provider. • A TCM charge related to a discharge that occurs during the 29-day period after the date of an earlier discharge. • E/M services on the same date as the required TCM face-to-face visit when rendered by the same provider or group practice, regardless if an E/M modifier is reported.
trigger_conditions: if a patient requires case management when transferring from a facility setting to the community or home setting

policy_title: Z-Code® Billing for Molecular Diagnostic Testing
rule_statement: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana requires a provider to report a molecular diagnostic test with a unique DEX Z-Code, as assigned by MolDX, and the applicable Current Procedural Terminology (CPT®) or Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) Level II code. Humana denies a molecular diagnostic test CPT or HCPCS code when it is not reported with the applicable DEX Z-Code. Providers should contact the MolDX program to register molecular diagnostic tests.
